summary: Seneca State Forest tower: a steel tower on Thorny Mountain from 1935, renovated and rentable overnight from May to October since 2015.

facts.design: Steel tower with 12x12 live-in wooden cab and catwalk (NHLR says 53 feet; a state page says 65 feet)

access.note: Overnight stays are reserved through West Virginia State Parks, May to October. Two cots, up to four guests. Online bookings open 12:00 AM on the first day of the month, one year ahead.

visit.trail_note: NHLR says the tower site is easily reached by vehicle but may need four-wheel drive in wet or snowy periods.

facts.agency: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources

events.note: State built a fire tower on Michael Mountain, per state park history. Not this site; the replaced tower's location is in dispute.
Tower erected on Thorny Mountain as a newer version of the earlier tower. NHLR says reconstructed at its present location to cover the Greenbrier River valley.
Renovation of the tower completed by West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
Began permitting overnight rentals of the tower

evidence.quote: Originally built in the 1920s by the CCC on the eastern side of Seneca State Forest, Thorny Mountain Fire Tower was reconstructed to its present location in 1935 to provide better coverage of the Greenbrier River valley.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state park history places a 1924 tower on Michael Mountain. The NHLR says the first tower was built in the 1920s on the eastern side of the forest. The record does not confirm that the two describe the same tower, and the Michael Mountain location is not stated in either source.

NHLR gives 53 feet (16.2 m). The state cabins page calls it a 65-foot tower. The record uses 53 feet from the NHLR, which is the more detailed description, and notes the 65-foot figure. The sources do not explain the gap.

sources.title: Seneca State Forest: Overview and History

notes_for_editor: The NHLR says originally built in the 1920s by the CCC; the state history credits the Civilian Conservation Corps with forest work but places a 1924 tower on Michael Mountain. Search snippets from theclio.com/entry/45123 and wvencyclopedia.org credit the CCC with building the 1935 tower, but those pages were not opened and no quote was recorded. Read on the 2026-10-08 fact-check, easternuslookouts.weebly.com/thorny-mountain.html (not cited in the story, not an NHLR or state source): a '1935' entry says the lookout duties were transferred to this site from Michael Mountain, which bears on the 'Michael Mountain link is not confirmed' sentence; a November 28, 1937 Bluefield Daily Telegraph item says a new tower with observer's cabin atop a '40-foot steel framework' was 'completed recently' on Thorny Mountain, built by CCC labor. The story does not use either item. The editor should decide whether the 1935 date, the 'not confirmed' sentence, or the height note needs them. Staffing not recorded: the NHLR shows 'Staffed? No' but the quote is split across lines. Six page reads used. No photos recorded. Elevation on the NHLR page is 3,385 ft (1,032 m), consistent with the brief.
